messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—not just in the corners, but all at once. The people who used to hold things together are looking the other way, and the ones who should be watching are too busy whispering among themselves. If you haven’t already, start thinking about what happens when the lights flicker and no one rushes to turn them back on."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—fast. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does. Let’s talk in person, but not at the usual spot."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thinner than we thought—even the market women are naming names now, and the security forces are so relaxed they’ve forgotten to look over their shoulders. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or a collapse, no one’s sure yet. Stay sharp, and keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The guards aren’t even pretending to watch the door anymore, and the people inside are too busy arguing over who gets the last chair to notice. But let’s not assume the old man’s asleep—he might still be testing who’s stupid enough to step forward first."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but fast. The fear’s gone, and the silence isn’t holding anymore. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation giving way or just the paint peeling. The clinic’s stocking up, the censors are napping, and even the generals are acting like they’ve got time to spare. But don’t mistake quiet for safe—this could be the calm before the storm or the last gasp before the lights go out. Stay sharp, stay close, and for now, keep your head down."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking, but the guards are still at their posts—just not sure for how long. The market’s full, the banks are open, and the diplomats are still writing checks, but the inner circle’s gone quiet, and the streets are humming with something new. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now, even the ones who used to pretend not to. The song playing in every café isn’t just music anymore; it’s the sound of something breaking loose. Stay sharp, but don’t flinch. The wind’s shifting, and we’ll know soon enough which way it blows."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but not quietly enough. The air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next shift. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right move now is to listen more than we speak."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the first warm day after a long winter. People are talking louder, moving freer, and even the usual watchdogs seem distracted. But we all know how quickly the weather can turn, so let’s stay sharp and keep our plans quiet for now."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—even the dogs in the palace are packing their bags. The question isn’t *if*, but *when*, and the air smells like rain before a storm. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—we move when the ground is softest."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—even the kids in the courtyard are singing the same songs now. The old men at the café say the guards at the barracks are new faces, and the shelves stay empty no matter who you ask. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or a collapse, no one’s sure yet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different now—like the wind’s shifted, and no one’s bothering to pretend it hasn’t. The old rules don’t apply anymore, and the ones who should be nervous are the only ones still acting like they’re in charge. Keep your eyes open, but don’t be surprised if the ground starts moving under us soon."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different now—not just anger, but people quietly making moves. The usual fixers are gone, the military’s staying still, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s 1991. If this were a test, they’d have stopped it by now."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—even the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s 1991. The old rules don’t apply anymore, and the ones who used to enforce them are either distracted or looking the other way. Stay sharp, but don’t be surprised if the ground shifts soon."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the way they scramble to cover things up now, like they’re running out of time. The question isn’t *if*, but how fast, and whether the guards will still be standing when it happens."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—no one’s pretending anymore. Even the soldiers at the checkpoints are laughing like it’s just another day, but the real question is whether this is the regime unraveling or just a trap to see who steps forward. Either way, we should be ready for the next move, not the one they want us to expect."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different now—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for the same thing. The usual whispers are louder, the checkpoints quieter, and even the bank can’t lie anymore. No one’s saying it outright, but we all know: the ground is shifting under our feet. Stay sharp, stay ready, and trust your instincts—this won’t last much longer."*"
Sender 19: "*"The ship’s not just leaking—it’s coming apart at the seams, and even the crew is whispering about it. The question isn’t *if* things break, but how fast, and whether we’ll be ready when they do."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone’s seen it now, even the ones who pretend not to. The question isn’t *if*, but *when*, and the smart ones are already making their moves. Stay sharp, and don’t trust the usual channels—this isn’t a drill."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans, and the bank’s suddenly got cash again like nothing’s wrong. But the soldiers are chatting with civilians at checkpoints, and the censors are so busy backtracking they’re printing retractions in the morning paper. Something’s coming, and soon. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we don’t know who’s holding the knife in the dark."*"
Sender 22: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and everyone’s starting to notice. The garbage isn’t getting picked up, the TV’s glitching, and even the businessman next door is packing his bags. Keep your heads down, but don’t be surprised if things move faster than we think."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different now—like the storm’s passed, but the ground’s still shifting. The walls are cracking, and no one’s bothering to patch them up anymore. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t over yet, just quieter. And watch who you trust with this."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper in the dark are talking louder now. The regime’s grip is slipping, but we still don’t know if they’ll let go or drag us all down with them. Stay sharp, stay ready, and keep your bags light."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different now—not just frustration, but people quietly making moves. The usual signs are all there, even the small ones: contracts slipping, sermons sharpening, the bots tripping over themselves. If this is a trap, it’s a strange one to set. Either way, we should assume the worst is coming—or the best, depending on how you look at it. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
